title: Stopped-short moves are reported successful
description:
Several authored finalizers treat idle as arrival despite having measured position and retaining a different requested target: `focuser_mypro2/indigo_focuser_mypro2.driver:333-338`, `focuser_dsd:215-217`, `focuser_dmfc:277-278`, `focuser_fc3:223-224`, `focuser_asi:207-208`, `focuser_usbv3:254-255`, and shared Lunatico rotator `focuser_lunatico/shared/lunatico_shared.c:889`. For example, mypro2 target1000, measured500 and moving0 enters the unconditional OK branch; the caller cannot distinguish target arrival from premature device stop. Shared Lunatico affects the rotator interface exposed by both focuser_lunatico and rotator_lunatico. Alpaca absolute focuser is excluded from this finding: its canonical class contract in `system_alpaca/indigo_system_alpaca_private.h` explicitly defines completion by IsMoving rather than comparing positions. Its deliberate settling window and idle completion are consistent with that accepted contract. A proposed target-equality finding there is rejected; changing the contract requires a separate explicit product decision. Remediation: distinguish commanded vs external/aborted motion, compare measured position with commanded expected position using protocol-appropriate tolerance/backlash semantics, publish ALERT on stopped-short and retain requested target. Add one early-stop regression per affected driver rather than assuming all protocols are identical. Existing exact-target handling in Astroasis, FLI, EFA, FocusDreamPro, Askar and SteelDrive2 shows a local behavior-preserving pattern.
